 NoGigiddy is seeking a proactive and customer-focused Entry-Level Account Manager to join our remote team. In this role, you will build and maintain relationships with our clients, ensuring their needs are met and providing exceptional service. This position is perfect for someone eager to start their career in account management and customer service. No college degree is required, but strong communication skills and a passion for helping clients are essential. 
   
   Key Responsibilities:  
   
 
 Client Relationship Management: Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, understanding their needs and ensuring their satisfaction. 
 Communication: Act as the main point of contact for clients, addressing their inquiries, concerns, and requests promptly and effectively. 
 Account Coordination: Assist in coordinating client accounts, including setting up new accounts, managing renewals, and ensuring all client information is up to date. 
 Problem Solving: Identify and resolve client issues proactively, ensuring a positive client experience. 
 Reporting: Prepare and deliver regular reports on account performance, client feedback, and service improvements. 
 Collaboration: Work closely with internal teams, including sales, marketing, and customer support, to ensure client needs are met. 
 Client Onboarding: Assist in onboarding new clients, providing them with the necessary resources and information to get started. 
 Feedback Collection: Gather and relay client feedback to improve our services and client experience. 
 
   Skills and Qualifications:   
 
 Communication Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. 
 Customer Service Skills: Strong ability to understand and meet client needs. 
 Organizational Skills: Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively. 
 Interpersonal Skills: Strong ability to build and maintain relationships with clients and team members. 
 Problem-Solving: Ability to address and resolve client issues effectively. 
 Time Management: Strong ability to manage time and meet deadlines. 
 Technical Skills: Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and CRM software. 
 
   
  Preferred Experience:  
   
 
 Experience in customer service, sales, or a related field is a plus but not required. 
 Familiarity with CRM software and account management tools is a plus. 
 Previous experience with gig economy platforms or staffing apps is a plus. 
 
  Education:  
 
 High school diploma or equivalent. 
 Relevant certifications or coursework in customer service, sales, or account management are beneficial but not required. 
 
  Working Conditions:  
 
 Remote Work: The role is remote, allowing for flexibility in work location. 
 Collaboration: Regular virtual meetings and communications with the sales and support teams. 
 Tools: Use of various communication and collaboration tools, such as email, video conferencing, and CRM software. 
 
  Salary Range:  
 
 $20 to $27 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications. 
 
  If you are organized, detail-oriented, and passionate about providing excellent service to clients, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to join NoGigiddy and make a difference in the gig economy.

  Location:  United States, Remote 
  This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

 Salesloft is building the next era of enterprise revenue — one where teams make confident decisions powered by AI and real signals. By combining our scale, insights, and AI innovation, we're building the industry's first Predictive Revenue System, enabling humans and AI to work together to make smarter decisions and drive consistent growth.

This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate. 
 Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

You will have a passionate, capable team supporting you.   
 You will be responsible for the support, development, and maintenance of Salesforce and its related Customer Experience systems. You must own the pursuit of a world-class technology experience for our customers, while enabling scale and efficiency for internal customer experience teams - Support, Services, and Success.  Work with Services, Success, and Support teams to identify manual process that can be automated

And in the spirit of how we are Customer Inspired — where every decision has a true north, and it's our customer — you'll administer access and configuration as the security controls they are, protecting the company and the data customers trust us with.

Team members conceptualize the strategic priorities for the company, develop execution plans, execute plans cross-functionally, and operationalize executed strategies for continuous improvement.

 Disciplined, flexible, and autonomous work habits; we don't micromanage

 Familiarity with NIST PQC standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FALCON) and lattice/hash-based cryptography fundamentals is a plus; 
 
 
 Understanding of quantum computing threats to elliptic curve cryptography and implications for key management in Web3;

 About SweetSpot Heating & Cooling  SweetSpot is a growing home-services company in the New York metro, and we are building our creative team from zero. This is the number one creative seat in the company, not a slot in a large agency hierarchy. The strategist hired here owns the function, works directly with the owner, and has a real path to leading the team as we scale.  About the role  We are hiring a creative strategist who will own paid ad creative end to end: research, angles, hooks, scripts, briefing creators and editors, and the learnings that turn winners into the next batch.  This is not a "make pretty ads" role and it is not strategy-only. You will direct really strong video editors and UGC creators, and you will use AI (including Claude Code) as your production engine for research, hooks, scripts and variants. We are honest about the level this role is hired at: we are looking for strong raw talent with real direct-response instincts who wants ownership and serious training, and who wants to grow into a top-tier strategist with us. You will get mentorship, a proven creative system, and weekly learnings reviews. In return we expect pace, curiosity, and work you can defend.  What you will do    Build the research base first: homeowner avatars, desires, objections, competitors, and our own ad account history. No angles before research.    Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency.    Write hooks and scripts built for the first 3 seconds: one desire, one avatar, one message per ad.    Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad.    Run the testing system: from one winning angle, build structured iterations where each variation tests something named.    Run the learnings: label every ad (Breakthrough, Spend Winner, KPI Winner, Loser), state why it performed, and turn that into the next round.    Hit 20 to 30 finished, launch-ready ads per month at full pace, working with our editors and AI workflows.    What we are looking for    Direct-response ad experience: you have written ads that ran as paid social (Meta or TikTok) and you can show them.    A testing system, not just good taste. You can explain how you turn one winner into 20 variations.    Research discipline. Your hooks trace to evidence, not guesses.    AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your creative workflow and can show how.    Execution: you have briefed creators or managed editors and shipped finished ads.    Ownership mindset: you talk about business outcomes, not just outputs delivered, and you close feedback loops: you learn, you apply, you show what changed.    Local services or lead generation experience is a plus, not a requirement. Seasonal urgency, emergency calls, proof and trust are the game here.    Pay and structure    Contract (1099), remote, month-to-month: $4,000 to $8,000 per month, 40 hours per week, based on experience.    Performance bonus structure discussed after the trial month, tied to winning ads.    Growth path: this seat grows into leading the creative team. One of the paths we model is editor or strategist to team lead as spend scales.    Our hiring process (exactly how it works)    Short application: portfolio of ads you wrote that actually ran, plus 3 short answers (your testing system on a real winner; one ad you iterated and what it tested; your AI workflow).    Interview 1 (30 minutes): screening and craft in one call, run as a working session on your past ads: what did you learn, how did you apply it, what feedback loops did you complete.    Paid test: $100 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours of work, paid regardless of outcome. A short research snapshot, hooks, scripts, an iteration plan and an execution plan for a real scenario.    Interview 2 (final, with the owner): we walk your test together and you defend your choices. References are checked after this call (we will ask to speak with one past employer). Two interviews total, no more.    Paid 30-day trial at your full agreed monthly rate, with daily contact, mentorship and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.    We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview. If you are the kind of strategist who would rather prove it than pitch it, apply.

jobs.title: Business Operations Manager
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.   
 Business Operations Manager  Remote (India) | Full-time 
 Also searched as: Operations Manager, Business Operations Lead, PMO Manager, Project Operations Manager, Shared Services Manager, GCC Operations Manager.  Could you lead ops coordinators, project managers and service teams while carrying real projects alongside them? On a typical day you might run the planning call for a cross-team project you are leading, review a dashboard showing which requests are running late, sit with a pod lead to rebuild an estimate that looks twice as long as the last similar job, and agree with the Internal Product team which manual handoff to automate next. 
 About Contour  
 We operate across three brands. The India team, part of the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building. It runs delivery, automation, people and operations for the whole organisation, working closely with teams in Australia. 
 
 The kind of people who thrive here  Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on. Today we are about 600 people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing.  The work matters. More than 10,000 students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. People who do well here care about that. They own their work end to end, start things without being asked and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, write decisions down and give direct feedback. The pace is fast: small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle. Growth follows what you deliver: scope, title and pay move with the bar you raise.  About this role You lead Operations in Contour's India team: several teams brought together under one player-coach. Your team includes Contour’s operations coordinators, who keep academics, campus, finance and the founder’s office running day to day, and its project coordinators and managers, who run cross-team work across the business. It also covers organisation services such as print operations, procurement and workspace systems. Each service has two sides. In Australia, a functional owner, such as Finance or Academics, sets its standards and priorities. In India, you run the work: coordinators and project managers report to you directly, and any service big enough for its own pod lead reports through them. Everything else is yours: how work comes in, how it is planned, checked and automated, and how the people doing it grow. Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you learn each service's workflow well enough to coach its lead, inspect what it produces and challenge its estimates, and you know where your knowledge stops: on professional questions, you rely on the specialists. Second, you make different services run as one, with a shared way of taking requests, planning capacity and checking work, so the rest of Contour deals with one group rather than a row of separate desks. This is a player-coach seat, and we mean it. Expect a real share of most weeks to go on doing the work yourself: running a cross-team project end to end, taking the coordination nobody else can untangle, checking a sample of finished work, mapping a process that keeps stalling or rebuilding an estimate from the ground up. The rest goes on making your coordinators, project managers and pod leads better at the same work. You won't be the specialist in every service, but you can work inside each one's workflow, and your team sees you do it. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: the scope of this seat grows with the platform, and what you deliver decides how fast. The intake, planning, quality and automation routines you set now are what every later service joins. What you will do 
 
 
 Run work yourself: lead some cross-team projects and coordination directly, especially the messy ones, so you know first-hand what your team is up against. 
 
 Lead the coordinators and project managers: set how projects and department requests are scoped, tracked and closed, review their plans and status updates, and step in when work slips. 
 
 Map every service's workflow with the people who run it and document it in Notion so anyone can follow it. 
 
 Run one front door for requests: a single intake form with clear turnaround times, so the rest of Contour deals with one group. 
 
 Plan capacity weekly using live dashboards of demand, turnaround and backlog, not gut feel. 
 
 Automate the repeatable: spot manual handoffs, data entry and status chasing, and work with the Internal Product team to automate them (for example with Monday, Notion, Slack, Google Workspace or no-code tools). 
 
 Use AI where it saves time: first-pass quality checks, drafting SOPs, summarising requests, with people keeping the final call.

About Swimply Swimply is the marketplace that lets homeowners rent out their private pools, hot tubs, courts and backyards by the hour. Thousands of hosts across the United States and Canada use Swimply to share space they already own with families and small groups in their community.    Because hourly backyard rentals are new, most local codes were written before they existed. Towns, counties, health departments and homeowners associations regularly try to fit Swimply into rules written for hotels, public pools, home businesses or overnight short-term rentals. We are building a dedicated regulatory function to manage those matters at scale and to move the rules in our favor, state by state.    You will own the day-to-day operation of the program and work directly with our General Counsel, our CEO, our Head of Operations and the outside lobbyists and local counsel we retain.    The Role  The Regulatory Affairs Manager runs Swimply's regulatory program end to end. Half of the job is operational: every notice a host or the company receives is logged, answered and tracked to a close. The other half is strategic: finding the bills, partners and officials that let us fix the rules for a whole state at once instead of town by town.   What You Will Do Run the notice program   Own the regulatory intake: the regulatory inbox, the host reporting form and escalations from the Host Success team.  Log every cease-and-desist letter, notice of violation, HOA demand and listing takedown in the regulatory tracker, by state, city, issuing agency and legal theory.  Sort each matter by the theory being used against us: public pool classification, home occupation or zoning, short-term rental rules, business licensing and tax, or HOA covenants.  Send the approved standard response to the host or code officer, and follow up until the matter is closed or escalated.  Escalate to the General Counsel within one business day anything involving a subpoena, a records demand, a lawsuit, criminal exposure or a threat to a whole market.  Publish a weekly regulatory report for the CEO and General Counsel: new notices, open matters, trends and recommended next steps.     Change the rules, state by state   Track bills and ordinances in our priority states, starting with New Jersey, New York, California and Texas, and flag any short-term rental or health-code bill our language could be added to.  Keep our model state bill and model city ordinance current.  Prepare the testimony, one-pagers, fact sheets and talking points our lobbyists and executives use with legislators and staff.  Reach out directly to selected city planning, code enforcement and health departments to explain our safety standards before a problem starts.   Manage outside firms and budget.  Day-to-day manager for our lead lobbying firm, state lobbyists and local zoning counsel: scopes, weekly updates, deadlines and invoices.  Build and maintain a bench of zoning counsel and lobbyists in each problem state, ready for when a matter escalates. jobs.title: Senior Pre-Sales & CSM US
jobs.description:
Description    About  Quicklizard      Quicklizard  is a pricing intelligence and optimization platform for retailers and brands. Our SaaS helps pricing, category and e-commerce teams set the right price across products, channels and markets, using competitive data, business rules and AI-driven recommendations to grow revenue and protect margin.  We are growing our customer base across the US and Latin America and are building a local team to serve and win customers in the region.    The role    We are hiring a hybrid pre-sales engineer and customer success manager to cover the Americas. The split is roughly 50/50: half your time managing and growing our US and Latin America customers, half supporting the sales team on new opportunities across the region.    This is a remote role, based in Mexico or the US  , reporting to the Director of Sales. You will work closely with Account Executives, our implementation and R&D teams, and product. Because you will sell and serve the same region, you own the full customer journey: from first demo to go-live, adoption and renewal.    What you'll do      Customer success (about 50%)    
 Own a portfolio of US and Latin America customers as their main day-to-day contact, from onboarding through renewal. 
 Lead onboarding and go-live: gather requirements, translate the customer's pricing logic into strategies and business rules, and coordinate data integration with our implementation and R&D teams. 
 Drive adoption: train users, spot underused capabilities, and recommend improvements to pricing strategies. 
 Run regular business reviews that tie  Quicklizard 's results to customer KPIs such as margin, revenue and price competitiveness. 
 Protect renewals by flagging risk early, and identify expansion opportunities (new categories, channels, countries or modules) together with the Account Executives. 
 Be the customer's voice internally, feeding requests and feedback to product. 
    Pre-sales (about 50%)    
 Partner with Account Executives on Americas opportunities, from discovery to signature. 
 Lead business and technical discovery: the prospect's pricing process, data sources, systems (ERP, e-commerce, POS) and competitive data needs. 
 Build and deliver tailored demos, workshops and proof-of-value environments, in English and Spanish. 
 Map prospect use cases to  Quicklizard 's pricing strategies, rules and integrations, and scope the implementation. 
 Own the technical and functional sections of RFPs, RFIs and security questionnaires. 
 Ensure a clean handover from sale to onboarding, so what we promise is what we deliver. 
    What you bring    
 5+ years of experience across pre-sales or solutions engineering, customer success and account management, in B2B SaaS or retail technology. 
 A background in retail: you understand how retailers and brands manage categories, promotions, pricing and assortment. 
 Technical fluency: comfortable with data, data feeds, APIs and system integrations, and able to speak with both IT and business stakeholders. 
 Strong demo and presentation skills, with confidence in front of pricing managers, category managers and C-level executives. 
 Fluent professional English and Spanish, written and spoken. 
 Based in Mexico or the US, with the right to work there, and available for regular travel to customers and prospects in the region. 
 A self-starter who works well remotely, across time zones, and is comfortable building processes in a region we are still growing. 
    Nice to have    
 Pricing experience: as a pricing analyst or manager at a retailer, or with price optimization, revenue management or competitive price monitoring software. 
 Familiarity with retail systems common in the region, such as SAP, Oracle, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify or VTEX. 
 Hands-on data skills (advanced Excel, SQL or Python) to build demo data and analyze customer results. 
 Experience with AI or machine-learning based products. 
 Portuguese, for customers and prospects in Brazil. 
 Experience working with a CRM such as HubSpot. 
    Why join us    
 Shape how  Quicklizard  sells to and serves customers across the Americas, at an early stage of our growth in the region. 
 A role that combines commercial and technical work, with direct impact on both new revenue and customer retention. 
 Work with a global, experienced team in retail pricing. 
 Fully remote from Mexico or the US, with a competitive compensation package.

jobs.title: Credit Data Assurance Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview    This is a remote role that will be hired in the Eastern Time Zone in the United States.  This position serves as a strategic partner across Credit, Reporting, Data, Product, and Technology organizations, ensuring business, data, process, and system changes are effectively assessed for impacts to Credit Reporting and downstream reporting deliverables.  This role is responsible for performing complex business and data impact assessments, translating business requirements into actionable data use cases, leading data triage, and root cause analysis efforts, and driving improvements in data quality, data lineage transparency, and reporting readiness. The analyst will play a critical role in proactively identifying and mitigating reporting and data risks.  The successful candidate will possess strong credit domain expertise, advanced analytical skills, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across multiple organizations while independently leading strategic initiatives.   Responsibilities & Qualifications    Duties & Responsibilities:  Credit Reporting Impact Assessment  
 Perform portfolio-level impact assessments to identify reporting, data, and operational risks before implementation. 
 Partner with business stakeholders to ensure reporting requirements are understood and incorporated into change initiatives. 
  Business & Data Requirements Management  
 Translate business requirements into credit data use cases and actionable requirements for Product, Technology, and Data teams. 
 Develop business process maps, data flow documentation, and reporting requirements to support strategic initiatives. 
 Act as a liaison between business users and technical teams to ensure alignment and successful delivery. 
  Data Analysis & Data Assurance  
 Perform advanced analysis of credit and reporting data to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities for improvement. 
 Improve transparency into data quality, data lineage, controls, and reporting readiness across the Credit Reporting ecosystem. 
 Support the design and implementation of processes that enhance data reliability and consumption confidence. 
  Data Triage & Issue Management  
 Lead data triage activities, root cause analysis, and issue prioritization across multiple stakeholder groups. 
 Coordinate the resolution of data quality, reporting, and operational issues by partnering with business, technology, and data teams. 
 Escalate and communicate material risks and issues to senior stakeholders as appropriate. 
  Reporting Risk Management  
 Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate reporting and data risks before they impact downstream consumers or regulatory deliverables. 
 Evaluate control effectiveness and recommend enhancements that strengthen reporting accuracy, completeness, and timeliness. 
 Support governance and risk management activities related to Credit Reporting and data management. 
  Strategic Leadership & Stakeholder Management  
 Independently lead cross-functional initiatives involving Credit, Reporting, Technology, Product, and Data organizations. 
 Influence decision-making by translating complex credit concepts into measurable business and data impacts. 
 Serve as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders on Credit Reporting, data risk, and reporting readiness matters. 
  Position Specific Skills:  
 Commercial Banking or Lending Operations Experience  
 Data Quality Management & Data Lineage  
 Cross-Functional Partnership & Collaboration  
 Data Analysis  
 Analytical Thinking  
 Risk Identification & Mitigation  
  Qualifications:   Bachelor's Degree and 4 years' experience OR High School Diploma or GED/Equivalent and 8 years' experience in Analytics, or Modeling, or Reporting   Preferred Qualifications:  
 Experience assessing the impact of data, process, system, or business changes on reporting and regulatory deliverables.  
 Strong understanding of commercial lending, credit products, and the end-to-end credit lifecycle.

 Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next. 
 We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd. 
 
 
  Why You’ll Love This Role  
 We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to help define and deliver Cribl security product experience. You will design for security practitioners across detection, alerting, investigation, triage, search, threat coverage, telemetry, and AI-assisted workflows. 
 This role requires a genuine security background and the ability to turn complex SOC workflows into clear, trustworthy experiences. You will partner with Product, Engineering, UX Research, and other designers to create a cohesive experience that works seamlessly with our other products across the entire Cribl platform.

 Design AI-assisted and agentic experiences that make intent, context, sources, capabilities, uncertainty, and user approval clear. 
 Use Cribl’s design system and contribute reusable components, patterns, guidance, and interaction models when the work has broader value. 
 Work expertly in Figma for exploration, prototyping, documentation, collaboration, and handoff, including libraries, variables, components, variants, and tokens. 
 Partner with engineers, PMs and designers through ideation, development to support feasibility, accessibility, resilience, and high-fidelity implementation challenges. 
 Share work early and often through critiques and working sessions. Give and receive specific, constructive feedback.
